newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries higher after firm overnight trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries higher after firm overnight trade.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities remained firm in overnight trading and opened higher on Wednesday with the Treasury's 30-year bond up 10/32.
Due this session at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT were new home sales and the Treasury's quarterly refunding announcement at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.

Analysts surveyed by Reuters expected, on average, that the total of three-year notes would be $16 billion, down from $17 billion in the last issue; 10-year notes would total $14 billion, up from $12 billion and the 30-year issue was expected to be unchanged at $10 billion.

"The market continues to retain its positive tone. The market is responding to the notion that there is no inflationary pressure on wages or prices," said Kevin Flanagan, money market economist and vice president at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.
With a bullish mindset continuing, Flanagan said it would likely take a very dramatic reading in one of the inflation indicators to buffet investors' optimism.
Supply has not proven to be a problem recently among the Wall Street community, so Flanagan said Wednesday's Treasury announcement probably would not disrupt the market.
"It just seems that every piece of information that comes out is on the favorable side," Flanagan said.
"The tone of the market is positive and that mood should continue with GDP tomorrow," said Kathleen Stephansen, senior economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp.
She said the deflator sections of the report should continue to show inflation contained.

"Barring any major surprises, the market should continue to perform very well, Stephansen said, although some profit-taking could be seen next week. This session likely would see little more price movement, she said.

At the short end of the maturity spectrum the three-month bill was one basis point lower at 5.09 percent. The six-month bill was unchanged at 5.12 percent and the year bill was two basis points lower at 5.16 percent.
The five-year note was up 5/32 at 100-5/32 to yield 5.96 percent, while the 10-year note was up 9/32 at 104-2/32 to yield 6.07 percent.
(( -- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1663 ))
